Poll question: In what ways is a greedy algorithm a special case of dynamic programming, and in what ways is it not? Explain your answer by relying on discussion points from today's session.
Answer:
Greedy is a special cafe of DP in the sense that both approaches rely on optimal substructure, the idea that optimal solution to a problem contains optimal solutions to its subproblem.

However, greedy is not a full case of DP because it never explores multiple subproblems while DP considers all possible options at each steps and builds up the globally optimal solution form overlapping subproblems.

Example of the coin game: Greedy pick the first highest value from either end while DP consider the highest value from the whole subarray to reach global optimal.

Instructor feedback: Good answer! You correctly identify optimal substructure as the common element and explain the key differences. To make your answer even better, you needed to explain how greedy becomes a special case of DP when certain conditions hold.
